first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMBs and has prior acquisition and revenue evidence. I would verify its qualification, margin, and retention outcomes, while comparing them with onboarding simplification’s downstream revenue evidence. The current intent is a guarded pricing test because discount-driven gains may not translate into sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified record shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline and failure through the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Continue with shortened onboarding. Its verified evidence improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue amid current activation and onboarding declines. The competitor’s deeper price cut raises urgency but does not reverse the verified finding that a 40% targeted discount attracted cohorts with 12% lower 30-day retention that failed to survive renewal. Promotional pricing is therefore too risky without a materially different, testable offer design.
